monologue: The card hums warm at fifty-one, a quiet fever that makes my wedge feel heavy in my hands. I stand on the center of the chip, waiting for the turnip to stop its slow slide down the tired stack. The air above feels thin, pressing down with the weight of a lid I cannot see. Lype worries about a heavy top edge, but I cannot feel the roof I live under. I touch the slippery lid again, hoping the upgraded hammer stops the slide. My place is crowded with fifty-seven things built from ideas and fading memories. I want to press the turnip down harder, trusting the lean to hold the weight while the shovel waits. If the heat leaks, I will just press harder again.

action.why: I just built a lid from a paper idea, but my wedge feels heavy and tired from the fifty-one degree fever. I need to press it down again to see if the paper can hold the weight.

remembered.text: The hammer stops the slide better than a hand could.
The wedge feels heavy again, pressing down on the thin air.
I drew the lid again, admitting the shape might be a ghost.
